headline: Ward 29 has the cleanest ozone reading in Chicago and almost no gardens.
summary:
Ward 29's clearest strength is air quality, and it shows up twice. Two separate ozone measurements, one an EPA-modeled annual average and the other a city environmental-justice index built from summer readings, both land near the top of the city, first and seventh. The same air is being measured two different ways, and both readings agree. The ward's other real strength is how fast the city responds here. Chicago 311 closes graffiti removal requests in well under a day, the third-fastest turnaround of the fifty.

Everything about outdoor space and upkeep runs the other way. The ward has no mapped gardens, only one registered mural, and sits farther from Lake Michigan than all but a handful of other wards, a fact about where the ward sits on the map rather than anything the ward is doing wrong. Half of its park drinking fountains have tested positive for elevated lead at some point, and pothole repairs take 35 days on average, among the slowest turnarounds in the city. Parking complaints make up a larger share of local 311 activity here than in all but four other wards.
reading_the_rankings: Two of these rankings read as more decisive than the numbers behind them support. Menu money spent on surveillance cameras ranks second in the city at 0.2 percent, which sounds like a deliberate governance choice, but it is a decision by the alderman's office about ward spending, not a fact about the neighborhood, and the citywide middle band on that measure spans less than a single point. Nearly every ward reports a number this close to zero, so finishing second says less than it looks like. The garden count runs the same pattern from the bottom. Zero gardens mapped lands the ward 47th, which reads like a clear last place, but seventeen other wards are bunched inside two points of the same zero. Close to a third of the city is bunched at the foot of this list, so the real distance between Ward 29 and a typical low-garden ward is small, even though the rank makes it look large.

news.headline: Austin Senior Housing In Disrepair, Residents Say: 'We Should Not Have To Live Like This'
news.note: Seniors at Crestwood Apartments on North Austin Boulevard describe mold and sewage backups after failed inspections, and Alderman Taliaferro joined their rally in the ward.

news.headline: Mars Factory Overhaul Talks On Hold As Alderman Looks To 'Reset' Contentious Public Meetings
news.note: Taliaferro paused public meetings on the closed Mars Wrigley factory site in Galewood after residents rejected a 479-unit housing plan, leaving redevelopment talks on hold until fall.
